The record of the extensions frozen at build (`META-INF/vauban-frozen-extensions.properties`, #288) now keeps what its fingerprint was computed from: the discovery settings and each bean class with its checksum (`settings=`, `class.<name>=`). A start whose fingerprint differs compares its deployment with the build's, and `ExtensionsAtStart.note()` names what differs instead of two opaque fingerprints:

```
the record of the frozen extensions (META-INF/vauban-frozen-extensions.properties) was written for another deployment: 1 bean class differs from the build's: com.acme.Extra (added)
```

Classes are listed as `(added)`, `(removed)` or `(changed)`, sorted, ten by name and the others counted; a change of the discovery settings is named first.

## Why

A refused record makes every build compatible extension run at start, silently: the note only gave two hashes, so nobody could tell which class or jar made the start differ from the build. Vidocq will log this note (WARN in a production launch, INFO in dev/test, and fail the start on demand), in a companion pull request on the same branch name.

## Compatibility

- A record written before this change has no `settings=` line: it is still used, its `deployment()` is `Deployment.UNKNOWN`, and its refusal note keeps the old fingerprint text.
- `FrozenExtensions` gains a `deployment` component (public record of `vauban-core`, used only by the container and the freeze).
- The container still logs the note at debug level: the embedding runtime knows whether a refused record is expected and says it at its own level.

## Tests

- `FrozenExtensionsRecordTest`: round trip of the deployment, an old record without the classes, the differences (added/removed/changed), the settings and a long list cut short.
- `FrozenExtensionsTest`: a changed deployment names the added class; a class that went away is named `(removed)`.
- Full reactor `-Pquality install` green; local SonarQube branch analysis: gate OK, 0 new issue.

Docs: `concepts.adoc` (what the record keeps, what a refusal note says), `whats-new.adoc`.
